title: Record the approved write-tool allow-list and set it in the AWS deployment config
description: The CISO and CTO review which ExampleCo agents call mcp-gateway and whether any of them needs a create, update or delete tool. The app README describes query-only use, so the expected result is an empty list. Record the decision in applications/mcp-gateway/repos/mongodb-mcp-server/deploy/aws/README.md: add a row for MDB_MCP_ALLOWED_WRITE_TOOLS to the environment-variable table (lines 40-50) with the approved value, the approver and the decision date. In deploy/aws/Dockerfile, next to `ENV MDB_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS=atlas-local` (line 13), add `ENV MDB_MCP_ALLOWED_WRITE_TOOLS=<approved list>`. If the approved list is empty, also add `ENV MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY=true`. Keep the default confirmationRequiredTools; do not shorten them. If any write tool is approved, it must also be in confirmationRequiredTools. PR to main with one non-author approval. Deployment happens in task 4.
acceptanceCriteria: deploy/aws/Dockerfile on main contains an `ENV MDB_MCP_ALLOWED_WRITE_TOOLS=` line matching the approved list, plus `ENV MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY=true` when that list is empty (check with `grep -n 'MDB_MCP_' deploy/aws/Dockerfile`)
deploy/aws/README.md has a table row for MDB_MCP_ALLOWED_WRITE_TOOLS naming the approved value, the approver and the decision date
Every tool in the approved allow-list is also covered by confirmationRequiredTools, confirmed by comparing the Dockerfile env with the userConfig.ts defaults or overrides in the PR
The PR is merged with an approving review from someone other than the author

verificationMethod.description: Re-run probe-agent-graph on mcp-gateway/mongodb-mcp-server at the merged commit. Expected: the deploy/aws tree configures deny-by-default (the allow-list set, and read-only when no write tools are approved), and neither AGENT-ASI02-01 nor AGENT-ASI09-01 is produced for the repo.

rootCause.description: The AWS deployment config (deploy/aws/Dockerfile) sets only MDB_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS=atlas-local and never restricts write tools. No approved list says which destructive capabilities agents may use.
